# LFM IQ Streamer (Generated by Claude)

Simulates the baseband IQ output of a pulsed radar receiver: complex white noise plus
delayed, Doppler-shifted LFM echoes from configurable point targets. It streams the result
continuously over UDP, paced to the sample rate.

## Layout

```
lfm_iq_streamer/
├── CMakeLists.txt
├── app/main.cpp                          streamer entry point
├── config/radar_sim.ini                  default parameters (copied next to the exe on build)
├── include/radarsim/
│   ├── protocol/                         shared with receivers (no sockets, no config)
│   │   ├── Constants.hpp
│   │   ├── LfmWaveform.hpp               chirp equation + matched-filter reference
│   │   └── PacketFormat.hpp              UDP wire format: serialize() / parse()
│   └── sim/                              simulator only
│       ├── Config.hpp  SignalGenerator.hpp  Streamer.hpp  UdpSender.hpp
└── src/
    ├── protocol/  Constants.cpp  LfmWaveform.cpp  PacketFormat.cpp
    └── sim/       Config.cpp  SignalGenerator.cpp  Streamer.cpp  UdpSender.cpp
```

The build defines three targets:

| Target | Contents | Who links it |
|---|---|---|
| `radarsim::protocol` | Packet format, LFM waveform, constants | Your listener |
| `radarsim::sim` | Config loader, signal generator, streamer, UDP sender | The streamer (and optionally your listener, to read the same .ini) |
| `lfm_iq_streamer` | Executable | Nobody; you run it |

## Build standalone

```
cmake -S . -B build
cmake --build build --config Release
./build/lfm_iq_streamer                 # finds config/radar_sim.ini next to the exe
./build/lfm_iq_streamer my_config.ini
```

## Use inside your own project (separate from your listener)

Copy this folder into your repo (for example `external/lfm_iq_streamer`), then in your top-level CMakeLists.txt:

```cmake
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(my_radar LANGUAGES CXX)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/bin)   # both exes land in build/bin

add_subdirectory(external/lfm_iq_streamer)   # provides lfm_iq_streamer + radarsim::protocol
add_subdirectory(listener)                   # your code
```

And in `listener/CMakeLists.txt`:

```cmake
add_executable(listener main.cpp)
target_link_libraries(listener PRIVATE radarsim::protocol)
```

Set `-DRADARSIM_BUILD_STREAMER=OFF` to build only the libraries.

## Signal model

**Transmitted pulse (baseband LFM, up-chirp from -B/2 to +B/2):**

    s(t) = exp( j·2π·( -B/2·t + (k/2)·t² ) ),   0 ≤ t < T,   k = B/T
    f_inst(t) = -B/2 + k·t

**Received signal for pulse n** (fast time t, measured from that pulse's transmit instant):

    r_n(t) = Σ_targets A · s(t - τ_n) · exp( j·2π·f_d·(t - τ_n) ) · exp( -j·2π·f_c·τ_n )  +  w(t)

    R_n  = R_0 + v · n · PRI        (range updated once per pulse, "stop-and-hop")
    τ_n  = 2·R_n / c
    f_d  = -2·v / λ,   λ = c / f_c  (v > 0 means receding, which gives negative Doppler)
    A    = sqrt( P_noise · 10^(SNR_dB/10) )
    w    ~ CN(0, P_noise),   P_noise = 10^(noise_power_db/10)

Sampling is r_n[m] = r_n(m / f_s) for m = 0 … N_pri-1, where N_pri = round(PRI·f_s).
Delays are evaluated analytically, so fractional-sample delays are exact.

## UDP packet format (little-endian)

| Offset | Type | Field |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | u32 | magic `0x464C5149` ("IQLF" on the wire) |
| 4 | u16 | version (1) |
| 6 | u16 | header size (40) |
| 8 | u64 | sequence number (a gap means a dropped packet) |
| 16 | u64 | pulse index n |
| 24 | u32 | sample offset within the PRI (0 = transmit instant) |
| 28 | u32 | number of samples N in this packet |
| 32 | u32 | samples per PRI |
| 36 | u32 | flags: bit0 = first packet of pulse, bit1 = last |
| 40 | f32 × 2N | I0 Q0 I1 Q1 … |

## Receiver processing outline

1. Reassemble each PRI using `pulse_index` and `sample_offset`, and zero-fill any packets detected as dropped.
2. Build the reference `s[m] = s(m/f_s)` for m = 0 … ceil(T·f_s)-1, using the same equation as above.
3. Apply the matched filter as a correlation: `y[l] = Σ_m r[m+l]·conj(s[m])`. With FFTs, this is
   `y = IFFT( FFT(r, N) · conj(FFT(s, N)) )` with N ≥ N_pri + N_pulse. The peak at lag l
   gives τ = l / f_s and R = c·τ / 2.
4. Optionally, stack M pulses and take an FFT across pulses in each range bin. The peak bin gives f_d,
   and v = -f_d·λ / 2. The unambiguous span is ±PRF/2.
5. Detection: apply a threshold above the noise floor. CA-CFAR is the usual next step. The expected post-MF
   SNR is SNR_dB + 10·log10(N_pulse), and the program prints this at startup.

The receiver can raise its socket receive buffer (SO_RCVBUF, a few MB) so it doesn't drop bursts.
